headline: Scheduling logic for overlapping events, built in a week for $19.
ledeMetrics: OVERLAP WARNINGS · LIVE SHARED DB · COST CALCULATOR · $19 TOTAL
problem: The social activities program had overlapping time slots, durations, and locations, and four pricing models at once — free, tip-based, pay-at-meeting-point, and pay-in-advance. The final activity list locked only about a week before launch; until then, planning data lived across shifting spreadsheet versions.
constraint: Roughly one week from final data to launch. The team wanted something small and sufficient, not a heavier commerce platform — but it still needed scheduling-conflict logic and a live shared database.
decision: Ticket Tailor — the right call at MALTALINK — was evaluated and ruled out here: it only pays off when collecting payment directly, and most activities were free, tip-based, or paid in person. Same thread, opposite verdict. With source data unstable, the highest-leverage work was UX triage with the designer: essentials (time, duration, price, days) on the card surface, everything else behind a "More details" toggle, copy shaped with the content editor. Fillout AI carried the registration mechanics on one month of its paid plan.

evidence.caption: Card browsing grouped by payment type; the expanded state shows the triage line — what earned the surface vs the toggle.

result.label: RESULT
result.metrics: ~1 WEEK · $19 TOTAL · CONFLICT WARNINGS · LIVE SHARED DB
result.body: A fully custom registration experience — overlapping-event warnings, editable confirmation emails, auto-hiding of activities within two days of their start, and a running cost calculator for pay-at-meeting-point totals — delivered in about a week for $19 total, with strong informal praise from the team.

lesson: When source data is late and unstable, the highest-leverage work is deciding what belongs on the surface — not waiting for the data to settle.
